business_model.claim: Dorian LPG earns revenue by owning and operating Very Large Gas Carriers (VLGCs) that transport liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) by sea.

business_model.claim: Net pool revenues are distributed to participants based on pool points (reflecting vessel attributes such as cargo capacity, fuel consumption, and speed) and the number of days the vessel was on-hire in the pool.

risks.basis: Stated in P1, P2, and P4; the absence of any fixed charter outside the pool is explicitly confirmed in all three items.
risks.claim: All 22 vessels operate exclusively in the Helios Pool on short-term charters or spot voyages, with 99% of revenue from the pool, leaving no fixed-rate revenue buffer against spot-rate declines.
quotes: For the years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024 approximately 99%, 97% and 95% of our revenues, respectively, were generated through the Helios Pool as net pool revenues—related party.

Currently, all twenty-seven vessels from our fleet, including our six time chartered-in vessels, operate in the Helios Pool, which employs vessels on short-term time charters, COAs, or in the spot market, the latter of which exposes us to fluctuations in spot market charter rates.
As of October 30, 2026, all twenty-two of our VLGCs were employed in the Helios Pool, including our five time chartered-in vessels.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (industry data as of May 22, 2026) and P6 (Q3 2026 update); the risk-factor language is from P2.
risks.claim: The VLGC orderbook has reached 36.4% of the existing fleet, with 160 VLGCs/VLACs (14.4 million cbm) scheduled for delivery through 2030, which could erode the supply tightness underpinning current freight rates.
quotes: According to industry sources, in the VLGC sector in which we operate as of May 22, 2026, there were 427 vessels with an aggregate carrying capacity of 35.8 million cbm in the world fleet and 124 vessels (including 78 ammonia carriers) with 11.1 million cbm of capacity on order for delivery by the end of 2029.

a further 160 VLGCs/VLACs—equivalent to approximately 14.4 million cbm of carrying capacity—are scheduled for delivery through calendar year 2030, including 19 new orders placed during the third quarter.
the combined VLGC/VLAC orderbook has increased to around 36.4% of the existing fleet.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor and debt summary), P8 (new facility terms), and F1/F2 (balance-sheet and income-statement figures as of September 30, 2026).
risks.claim: Dorian carries $544.4 million of outstanding indebtedness with two credit facilities at variable rates; a sustained rise in interest rates or a drop in earnings could strain debt-service capacity.
quotes: As of May 22, 2026, we had outstanding indebtedness of $544.4 million, of which $465.0 million is hedged or fixed.

Two of our credit facilities bear interest at variable rates and we anticipate that any future credit facilities will also bear interest at variable rates. Increases in prevailing rates could increase the amounts that we would have to pay to our lenders or financing counterparties, even though the outstanding principal amount remains the same, and our net income and available cash flows would decrease as a result.
the Company entered into a new seven year $368.4 million credit facility to refinance existing indebtedness

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (Business section) and P2 (Risk Factors); the caveat about petrochemical demand reducing seasonality is also in both.
risks.claim: VLGC spot rates are highly seasonal, with historically weaker quarters in the first and second calendar quarters, and the company's fiscal year ends March 31, meaning its first half (fiscal H1, ending September 30) captures the stronger autumn/winter season while fiscal H2 faces the trough.
quotes: The LPG shipping market historically has been stronger in the autumn months in anticipation of increased consumption of propane and butane for heating during the winter months.

VLGC spot market rates are highly seasonal, typically demonstrating strength in the second and third calendar quarters as suppliers build inventory for high consumption during the northern hemisphere winter.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors section on Panama Canal).
risks.claim: Panama Canal transit restrictions and toll increases add unpaid waiting time and higher costs to VLGC voyages on the US Gulf-to-Asia route, an important trade lane for the company's customers.
quotes: The Panama Canal Authorities decreed that the slots for transit by VLGCs could only be reserved up to 14 days in advance of a proposed transit. This change has resulted in longer wait times and periods of high auction prices to reserve transits.

The Panama Canal Authority has periodically restructured its toll structure, which increased rates charged on tonnage for different vessel classes, including the VLGCs that cross the waterway, resulting in increased rates or additional waiting time for our VLGCs to cross the Canal.

risks.basis: Stated in P6 (CEO comment in earnings release); the broader operational risk language is in P2.
risks.claim: LPG-carrying vessels are being targeted in a turbulent geopolitical environment, posing safety and operational risks to the fleet and crew.
quotes: In a turbulent geopolitical environment when ships carrying LPG have been targeted, I am glad to report that our seafarers have been kept out of harm's way.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors); fleet age and scrubber data from P1 and P4.
risks.claim: Increasing ESG scrutiny, emissions regulations, and the U.S. Maritime Action Plan could impose additional costs or operational restrictions on the VLGC fleet.
quotes: Increasing scrutiny and changing expectations from investors, lenders and other market participants with respect to our Environmental, Social and Governance, or ESG, policies may impose additional costs on us or expose us to additional risks.

The U.S. government's Maritime Action Plan could result in new trade, regulatory or industrial policy measures affecting foreign-built vessels, which could increase our costs and affect our operations.
